hypotheses.statement: The receipt-first ledger erases no valid claim, including those whose evidence container is corrupt
The evidence-first behaviour erases the claims whose container is corrupt
Corrupt containers are kept, resends collapsed, conflicts and malformed input quarantined, oversize input refused and not counted as received
The R10 in-memory condition leaves overflow UNACKNOWLEDGED; the persistent ledger keeps every valid submission (12 ACTIVE and the rest QUEUED)
Concurrent submissions from four connections, a reopened database, the same claim id in another case and an invalid submission first do not lose or refuse valid submissions

targets: receipts, evidence, proceedings, plans, measurements and closures of a synthetic ledger

instrument_conditions.stream: 80 submissions per world: valid, corrupt container, resend, conflict, malformed, oversize

reproduction.world: xzr.teoo.lawledger (SQLite, append-only) on xzr.teoo.lawworld (8 Booleans); this implementation's own world, not Appendix O

L101.criterion: 0 valid or corrupt-container claims erased by the receipt-first ledger in every world

L102.contrast: claims erased per world: evidence first minus receipt first

L103.criterion: every corrupt container kept as a receipt, every resend collapsed, every conflict and malformed input quarantined, every oversize input refused and not received, in every world

L104.criterion: R10 (70 valid): 12 ACTIVE, 52 QUEUED, 6 UNACKNOWLEDGED; persistent (65): 12 ACTIVE, 53 QUEUED, 0 UNACKNOWLEDGED

L105.criterion: 4 connections x 6 concurrent submissions: 24 receipts, 24 distinct sequences, 0 errors, 12 ACTIVE and 12 QUEUED after reopening; the same claim id in another case is a separate receipt; a malformed submission first does not refuse the valid one after it

catalogue.source: The Minimum Guarantees of Human Legal Subjecthood, Publication Final V3.0, Chapter 6.2 (identical in the 100_POINT_EDITION and in R2 section 4: all fifteen titles and definitions compared character for character)
catalogue.note: V3.0 uses two vocabularies for the same five findings (Appendix A table: Secured/Partial/Absent/Indeterminate/Inapplicable; A.3 and 8.4 text: Satisfied/Partially Satisfied/Failed/Indeterminate/Not Applicable). R2 section 16 and this implementation use the table's.

note: results about a SYNTHETIC ledger and this implementation's own world; the manuscripts R5-R16, the historical code and the world of Appendix O were not available and their numbers are not reproduced; a closure, a measurement or a match here is not a legal judgment or a restoration; not an observation of any institution, law or person
